title: RCTD: Reputation-Constrained Truth Discovery in Sybil Attack Crowdsourcing Environment

problem.claim: Truth discovery in crowdsourcing must infer trustworthy information from conflicting data while addressing Sybil attacks and quality-control concerns.

gap.claim: Existing truth discovery approaches overlook workers' historical reputations, including approval rates that are noisy and inflated but may indicate worker ability.

contributions.claim: RCTD refines worker approval rates with the Wilson Lower Bound and reduces their noise and inflation using ranking similarity.

RCTD introduces a similarity metric between worker-weight rankings and refined approval-rate rankings, using it as a penalty to constrain estimated weights from deviating excessively from historical reputation.
The objective function is solved with block coordinate descent coupled with a heuristics approach.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on real-world datasets reportedly show more accurate inference of true results than state-of-the-art methods in the Sybil attack environment.

narrative_sequence.summary: Sybil attacks create a crowdsourcing quality-control concern, and truth discovery infers trustworthy information from conflicting data.
Existing approaches omit workers' historical reputations despite their noisy and inflated approval rates providing a rough ability signal.
The approach refines approval rates, mitigates their noise and inflation, and constrains worker weights using ranking similarity.
The resulting objective is solved using block coordinate descent with heuristics.
Real-world dataset experiments reportedly outperform state-of-the-art methods in inference accuracy under Sybil attacks.

source_observation.claim: Historical reputation is incorporated as a penalty that limits excessive divergence between estimated worker weights and reputation-derived rankings.

interpretation.claim: Noisy auxiliary reputation signals may be useful when confidence-adjusted and integrated as constraints rather than treated as direct truth.

application.claim: In other conflicting-data inference settings, refine historical reliability indicators and use ranking-based regularization to stabilize contributor weighting.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this strategy works beyond the reported Sybil attack crowdsourcing environment or datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the real-world datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the Sybil attack model, threat assumptions, or parameter settings.
The abstract does not provide algorithmic details sufficient to assess convergence, complexity, or implementation reproducibility.
